question:
RR 25->26 (band=mild_tachypneic)
A 26-year-old woman reports to her physician with complaints of difficulty breathing. She notes that her
symptoms typically occur when she is outdoors and improve with rest and staying indoors, but they are
currently more severe than usual. She has no prior medical history and has never consulted a
physician before. Her vital signs include a temperature of 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure of 119/59
mmHg, pulse of 113/min, respirations of 26/min, and oxygen saturation of 88% on room air. Pulmonary
function tests reveal decreased inspiratory and expiratory flow rates. What is the most appropriate
initial treatment for this patient? Answer Choices: (A) Magnesium sulfate (B) Ipratropium bromide (C)
Cromolyn sodium (D) Terbutaline (E) Methylprednisolone (F) Racemic epinephrine (G) Epinephrine (H)
Oxygen therapy alone (I) Albuterol (J) Diphenhydramine
 A. Methylprednisolone
B. Ipratropium bromide
C. Albuterol
D. Racemic epinephrine
E. Terbutaline
F. Cromolyn sodium
G. Oxygen therapy alone
H. Magnesium sulfate
I. Diphenhydramine
J. Epinephrine
